howto.title: How to play
howto.0.title: Goal: the most prim
howto.0.text:
• Everyone starts with {0} prim. Prim is your money and your score.
• At the end, the player with the most prim who was not fired wins.
• Balances are hidden: everyone sees only their own prim.
• There are no role cards; anyone can be a little bad.
howto.1.title: Match flow
howto.1.text:
• Tasks 1 and 2: in pairs (one trio when the count is odd).
• Then meeting 1: failed tasks are voted on.
• Task 3: everyone together. If the shift is short, meeting 2 (no vote: the skippers get blame).
• Then the Crisis, and finally the Final: someone is fired.
• A match takes 12–15 minutes.
howto.2.title: Task: Client Bonus
howto.2.text:
• You and your group choose in secret: Share or Take it all.
• If you both share: {0} prim each.
• If one takes: the taker gets {1}, the sharer {2}. If both take: {3} each.
• Only your group sees who took; the others only learn how many took.
• A sharer can investigate the taker for free in meeting 1: the taker keeps the prim but gets +{4} blame.
howto.3.title: Task: Petty Cash and whistling
howto.3.text:
• You can secretly take prim from the cash. If you are the only taker in your group: +{0} prim.
• If two take at once, both are caught: no prim, +{1} blame each.
• Your group-mate is a witness and may whistle on you in the break. Whistling is free and earns the whistler nothing.
• A whistled thief keeps the prim but gets +{2} blame.
• The witness may also keep quiet or bargain on the phone ("keep quiet and I'll send you 1 prim"); promises are not binding.
howto.4.title: Task: Weekend Shift
howto.4.text:
• Everyone chooses in secret: take the shift or skip it.
• Taking the shift pays no prim but lowers your blame by {1} (never below zero).
• Half the players are needed on the shift. If enough take it, skipping pays +{0} prim.
• If too few take it, the task fails: skippers get no prim and +{2} blame in meeting 2, without a vote.
• Everyone sees who took the shift.
howto.5.title: Blame and the blame vote
howto.5.text:
• Blame is public and decides who becomes a candidate in the final.
• If a task failed, meeting 1 holds a secret blame vote: everyone gets 1 ballot per failed task.
• Each ballot gives its target +{0} blame. You cannot vote for yourself.
• You cannot abstain: an empty ballot goes to yourself.
• If nothing failed, there is no vote. A short shift has no vote either: the skippers get their blame automatically.
howto.6.title: Investigation
howto.6.text:
• Once, in meeting 1, you can open an investigation: only if you shared the Client Bonus and your group-mate took it all.
• It is free and earns you no prim.
• The result is shown to everyone: the taker gets +{0} blame and keeps the prim they took.
• The taker may offer you prim to keep quiet; promises are not binding.
howto.7.title: Phone, recorder and leaks
howto.7.text:
• In the office you only talk 1:1 by phone. In meetings everyone hears everyone.
• The line board shows who talks to whom, never what they say.
• You can secretly record a call ({0} time(s) per match); the other side is not told.
• Leak it in a meeting and {1} seconds of it play for everyone.
howto.8.title: Transfers and promises
howto.8.text:
• You can send prim to anyone at any time (at most {0} at once).
• Only sender and receiver see a transfer; all are revealed at the end.
• Promises are not binding: "I'll vote for you" or "I'll pay" may be lies.
• Who pays first? This is where the recorder helps.
howto.9.title: Crisis and candidates
howto.9.text:
• In the Crisis, {0} blame goes to one player by secret vote; a tie splits it.
• Before the vote only phones are open: bargain. An empty ballot goes to yourself.
• Then the players with the most blame become firing candidates ({1} with 3–4 players, {2} with 5–6); everyone tied for the last place is a candidate too.
• Nobody with 0 blame is a candidate; with fewer candidates, fewer are fired.
• Candidates' desks are sealed: they cannot send prim, but they can receive it.
howto.10.title: Final and firing
howto.10.text:
• Candidates defend in turn, then everyone secretly votes for one candidate.
• The most voted is fired ({0} with 3–4 players, {1} with 5–6). A tie gets one revote.
• The fired player's desk is opened: their prim is split equally among those who voted for them; the remainder burns.
• You may abstain, but then you get no share.
• At the end every ballot, transfer and choice is revealed.
howto.11.title: Pranks
howto.11.text:
• In the meeting, {6} opens the quick wheel (or the folder's Pranks tab): coffee, paper plane, post-it, ringing a phone, slurping tea, standing up, buttering up the boss.
• Some are free, some cost prim (coffee {2}, phone {3}); prim spent is burned, nobody gets it.
• Every prank uses up the boss's patience. At {0}, whoever did the last one is written up (+{1} suç). A phone ring's target is written up; who rang it comes out at the results.
• During the defence patience goes ×{5}; buttering him up eases it by {4}.
• Sealed candidates cannot spend prim; the fired wait for the results. At the results anyone may throw cake.
• No prank ever blocks a vote, voice or the defence.
